causal_attribution.original_claim: Both sub-hypotheses are rejected (causal_hypothesis_holds=false, both hypothesis_breakdown entries set holds=false)
causal_attribution.corrected_conclusion: Only the JOINT strategy of max-LPIPS proposal selection AND early-scale-biased time sampling is observed to underperform baseline (FID 10.127 vs 9.663) in this single fixed-run comparison. Because both design factors were changed simultaneously relative to baseline, there is no isolation evidence to reject either sub-hypothesis individually. The degradation could come from either factor alone or their interaction. Both sub-hypotheses remain plausible but untested in isolation.
single_trial_limitations: One joint comparison cannot decompose two simultaneous factor changes into individual causal contributions.
No statistical replication — the FID difference is a single 50k-sample evaluation, not a distribution of runs.
The baseline is a published reference, not re-run under identical evaluation conditions in this round.
Cannot conclude by flipping both factors in round-02 whether the improvement (if any) came from selection direction, time distribution, or their interaction.

retained_guesses.max_lpips_may_be_harmful: Plausible but unisolated: hard-example selection at 256 samples may select noisy outliers.
retained_guesses.early_bias_may_be_harmful: Plausible but unisolated: early-scale concentration may starve later scales at low sample count.

causal_attribution.next_round_caveat: The planned round-02 (min-LPIPS + uniform time) is still a reasonable diagnostic step, but its result will only answer whether the opposite joint configuration is better — it will not by itself isolate which single factor was responsible. Two further single-factor-perturbation runs would be needed for full isolation, which may not be worth the budget.
